scaling_diagnosis.phase_timing_environment: FEREG_PHASE_TIMING=1; same clean release binary, not LLVM coverage instrumentation
scaling_diagnosis.units: seconds, except schur*.iterations, schur_route.contraction and fit.residual_overlap
phase_interpretation: Uninstrumented total estimation median increases from 0.043 s at 8 threads to 0.053 s at 16; M2 also increases from 0.043 to 0.051 s.

With existing phase timers, fit total medians are 0.016923 and 0.023147 s. Initial absorption increases about 2.527 ms, QR finite solve 0.974 ms, residual/bread overlap 1.221 ms, and RHS/setup 0.637 ms. Medians are independently computed and need not add.

Schur is selected throughout. At 8 and 16 threads the initial solve uses 2 iterations, final residual projection 0, and residual overlap is enabled. No observed 8-to-16 route switch or iteration increase.
Schur route probe rises from 3.205 to 4.432 ms, inside the initial-absorption interval. Nested timings must not be added to their parent.

Initial absorption includes its certification/result handling. RHS interval also includes FE session setup and admission. bread_raw_residual includes concurrently overlapped residual projection/score, so tiny residual_absorb does not mean that residual projection is free.

Stata command timing excludes process startup and data loading. Input loading medians in the timed diagnostic are 8.769/9.140 ms; host prepare is 4.073/4.272 ms. Outputs/shadow/inference statistics are small; the rise is predominantly native fitting. Thread-pool setup can remain inside native timing.
Scheduler overhead, task granularity, cache/memory traffic and hardware placement remain hypotheses. Timers localize work but do not identify a hardware root cause.
scaling_diagnosis.proposed_next_scope: Audit Schur probe/full-solve preparation and repeated level reductions. Choose one shared kernel or removable repeated setup stage with code and timing evidence; preserve weighted operator, probe, certificates, fallbacks and memory admission. Do not remove the probe or change routes merely because it costs time.

limits: Local small/medium bounded campaigns, not universal functionality or performance proof.
No new Windows next build, licensed Windows run, SCC large-data or 28-thread campaign in M3-M7. Existing platform/package contract is unchanged.
No release bundle or public native distribution qualification; mixed local staging keeps older other-platform next artifacts.
M7 diagnoses the existing slowdown; it does not implement a speed fix or M8.
No broad solver, representation or fast/low pipeline consolidation is claimed.
